title: Quick check: Prompt Testing and Optimization

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes creating a prompt test set in the context of prompt testing and optimization?
options: Use the largest available model for every task and skip a baseline or documented acceptance criteria.

Treat creating a prompt test set as part of the model's input contract: state the task, provide only relevant context, specify what a good response looks like, and test representative and ambiguous cases. A prompt can guide behavior, but application code must still validate important outputs.
A fluent result is enough to establish correctness, so the input and assumptions do not need checking.
The concept can be implemented entirely in a prompt; application validation and testing are unnecessary.
questions.answer_key: Treat creating a prompt test set as part of the model's input contract: state the task, provide only relevant context, specify what a good response looks like, and test representative and ambiguous cases. A prompt can guide behavior, but application code must still validate important outputs.
questions.explanation: Treat creating a prompt test set as part of the model's input contract: state the task, provide only relevant context, specify what a good response looks like, and test representative and ambiguous cases. A prompt can guide behavior, but application code must still validate important outputs. This is why the lesson treats the concept as something to apply and verify, not as a guarantee of quality.

questions.prompt: Which practice gives the clearest evidence that defining expected output characteristics is working in prompt testing and optimization?
options: Use representative cases, an explicit success criterion, and retained failure examples; compare results against a baseline before relying on the behavior.
Test only one easy input, then assume the behavior generalizes to every language, user, and data source.
Skip validation because a well-formatted answer implies the model followed the intended process.
Change the prompt, model, data, and settings at the same time, then attribute any difference to one cause.
questions.answer_key: Use representative cases, an explicit success criterion, and retained failure examples; compare results against a baseline before relying on the behavior.
questions.explanation: Defining expected output characteristics should be evaluated with evidence appropriate to its use. Representative tests and a baseline help reveal failures and avoid overstating what the example proves.

questions.prompt: A team applies creating a prompt test set from prompt testing and optimization and gets a plausible result, but it has not checked an edge case. What should it do next?
options: Accept the result because confidence and fluency are reliable substitutes for measurement.
Remove guardrails or access checks to make the next run more likely to succeed.
Increase model size and deploy immediately, without retaining a baseline or regression tests.
Reproduce the case with controlled input, check source/evidence and intermediate steps where available, test an edge case, and document remaining uncertainty.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the case with controlled input, check source/evidence and intermediate steps where available, test an edge case, and document remaining uncertainty.
questions.explanation: A plausible answer is not proof. Controlled tests, evidence checks, and explicit uncertainty help identify incorrect assumptions and unsafe failure modes.
